'''Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc.''' is an American life science and clinical research company. It is a global supplier of analytical instruments, clinical development solutions, specialty diagnostics, laboratory, pharmaceutical and biotechnology services. Based in [[Waltham, Massachusetts]], Thermo Fisher was formed through the [[Mergers and acquisitions|merger]] of [[Thermo Electron]] and [[Fisher Scientific]] in 2006. Thermo Fisher Scientific has acquired other reagent, consumable, instrumentation, and service providers, including [[Life Technologies (Thermo Fisher Scientific)|Life Technologies Corporation]] (2013),<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gelles |first1=David |title=Thermo bid wins Life Technologies auction |url=https://www.ft.com/content/a3466cfc-a5c8-11e2-9b77-00144feabdc0 |newspaper=Financial Times |date=15 April 2013 |access-date=29 November 2021}}</ref> [[Alfa Aesar]] (2015),<ref>{{cite web |last1=Seiffert |first1=Don |title=Thermo Fisher to buy 480-employee chemical maker based in Haverhill |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/boston/blog/bioflash/2015/07/thermo-fisher-to-buy-480-employee-chemical-maker.html |website=bizjournals.com |date=July 22, 2015 |publisher=Boston Business Journal |access-date=29 November 2021}}</ref> [[Affymetrix]] (2016),<ref>{{cite web |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to Acquire Affymetrix for $1.3B |url=https://www.genengnews.com/news/thermo-fisher-scientific-to-acquire-affymetrix-for-1-3b/ |website=genengnews.com |date=11 January 2016 |publisher=Genetic Engineering & Biotechnology News |access-date=29 November 2021}}</ref> [[FEI Company]] (2016),<ref>{{cite news |last1=Picker |first1=Leslie |title=Thermo Fisher to Acquire FEI for $4.2 billion |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/05/28/business/dealbook/thermo-fisher-to-acquire-fei-for-4-2-billion.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |date=27 May 2016 |access-date=29 November 2021}}</ref> [[BD (company)|BD Advanced Bioprocessing]] (2018),<ref>{{Cite web |last=Writer |first=GEN Staff |date=2018-09-07 |title=Thermo Fisher Acquiring BD's Advanced Bioprocessing Business |url=https://www.genengnews.com/news/thermo-fisher-acquiring-bds-advanced-bioprocessing-business-2/ |access-date=2022-08-09 |website=GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[PPD, Inc.|PPD]] (2021).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Completes Acquisition of PPD, Inc. |url=https://ir.thermofisher.com/investors/news-events/news/news-details/2021/Thermo-Fisher-Scientific-Completes-Acquisition-of-PPD-Inc/default.aspx |access-date=2022-08-09 |website=ir.thermofisher.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

It ranked 106th on the [[Fortune 500|''Fortune'' 500]] list based on its 2025 annual revenue of $44.556 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fortune 500 |url=https://fortune.com/ranking/fortune500/ |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref>

== History ==

=== Predecessors and merger ===
[[Thermo Electron]] was co-founded in 1956 by [[George N. Hatsopoulos]] and Peter M Nomikos. Hatsopoulos received a PhD from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] in [[mechanical engineering]] and Nomikos was a [[Harvard Business School]] graduate.<ref>[https://news.mit.edu/2018/george-hatsopoulos-senior-lecturer-emeritus-mechanical-engineering-thermo-electron-founder-dies-0921 George Hatsopoulos, senior lecturer emeritus and MIT Corporation life member emeritus, dies at 91] ''"Thermodynamics expert and longtime Department of Mechanical Engineering affiliate founded Thermo Electron, a world leader in instrumentation... ...along with Peter Nomikos, he co-founded the Thermo Electron Corporation"'' 21 September 2018 ''web.mit.edu''</ref>  The company focused on providing analytical and laboratory products.

[[Fisher Scientific]] was founded in 1902 by Chester G. Fisher from [[Pittsburgh]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/PPG+Vice+President+Fisher+Dies.-a091223616|title=PPG Vice President Fisher Dies.|work=thefreelibrary.com|access-date=July 17, 2013|archive-date=March 5, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305024603/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/PPG%20Vice%20President%20Fisher%20Dies.-a091223616|url-status=dead}}</ref> It focused on providing laboratory equipment, chemicals, supplies and services used in healthcare, scientific research, safety, and education.<ref name="ir.thermofisher.com">{{cite web|url=http://ir.thermofisher.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=89145&p=irol-homeProfile|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific : Corporate Profile<!-- Bot generated title -->|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070703141935/http://ir.thermofisher.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=89145&p=irol-homeProfile|archive-date=2007-07-03}}</ref>

On May 8, 2006, Thermo Electron and Fisher Scientific announced that they would [[Mergers and acquisitions|merge]] in a tax-free, stock-for-stock exchange; the merged company was named Thermo Fisher Scientific, and had about 30,000 employees, and reported US$9 billion in combined revenue.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bloomberg News |date=2006-05-09 |title=Deal by Lab Equipment Makers Priced at $10.6 Billion in Stock |newspaper=The New York Times |page=C00005 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/05/09/business/deal-by-lab-equipment-makers-priced-at-106-billion-in-stock.html |access-date= 2023-07-23}}</ref> On November 9, 2006, the companies announced that the merger had been completed.<ref name="ReferenceA">[http://ir.thermofisher.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=89145&p=irol-newsArticle&ID=929319&highlight= Merger of Thermo Electron and Fisher Scientific Completed, Forming Thermo Fisher Scientific] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120722153658/http://ir.thermofisher.com/phoenix.zhtml?c=89145&p=irol-newsArticle&ID=929319&highlight= |date=2012-07-22 }}, press release, November 9, 2006</ref> However, the [[Federal Trade Commission]] ruled that this acquisition was anti-competitive regarding [[centrifugal evaporator]]s, requiring Fisher to divest [[Genevac]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2006-10-17 |title=Thermo Electron Corporation, In the Matter of |url=https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings/0610187-thermo-electron-corporation-matter |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=Federal Trade Commission |language=en}}</ref>  In April 2007, Genevac was sold to Riverlake Partners LLC<ref>3 April 2007. [http://www.riverlakepartners.com/documents/Genevac_Final_Press_Release.pdf Riverlake Partners, LLC Acquires UK-based Genevac, Ltd.] Press Release.</ref> and the merger closed with FTC approval.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-03-30 |title=FTC Approves Proposed Divestiture in Matter of Thermo Electron Corporation |url=https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2007/03/ftc-approves-proposed-divestiture-matter-thermo-electron-corporation |access-date=2024-01-25 |website=Federal Trade Commission |language=en}}</ref>

The company's products are sold under the brand names of Thermo Scientific, Fisher Scientific, and several other recognized brand names (e.g. Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen, [[Patheon]], [[PPD, Inc.|PPD]], and [[Nalgene]]).

=== Acquisition history ===

In 1990, Thermo Fisher Scientific (then known as Thermo Instrument Systems) acquired mass spectrometer manufacturer Finnigan Instrument Corporation.<ref>{{cite news |title=COMPANY NEWS; Thermo Unit Sets Deal for Finnigan |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1990/04/25/business/company-news-thermo-unit-sets-deal-for-finnigan.html |access-date=25 May 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=25 April 1990}}</ref>

In 2003, the company (then Fisher Scientific International) acquired Perbio Science, a transaction that included brands such as Pierce Biotechnology, HyClone and Endogen.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/pittsburgh/stories/2003/06/23/daily48.html |title=Fisher Scientific buying Perbio Science for $714M|access-date=25 May 2024 |work=www.bizjournals.com |date=26 June 2003}}</ref>
In April 2006, BioImage was acquired by Thermo Fisher Scientific.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thermo Scientific - US|url=https://www.thermofisher.com/us/en/home/brands/thermo-scientific.html|access-date=2021-02-04|website=www.thermofisher.com|language=en}}</ref> The merger was complete in November 2006, and technology transfer to a US site was completed during 2007 and 2008.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Life Technologies|url=http://www.bioimage.com/pdf/CEOletter.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080517075244/http://www.bioimage.com/pdf/CEOletter.pdf|archive-date=2008-05-17|access-date=2017-04-24|website=BioImage|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=BioImage Company Profile: Acquisition & Investors|url=https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/54708-49|access-date=2021-02-04|website=PitchBook|language=en}}</ref> BioImage was established in 1993 as a drug discovery research unit led by Ole Thastrup within [[Novo Nordisk]], from which it spun out of in 1999. It had specialized in developing and selling proprietary [[bioassay]]s to [[biopharmaceutical]] companies and research institutions. It made broad [[patent]]s covering [[EGFP|Enhanced GFP]] (EGFP), GFP-based biosensors and any genetically encoded [[Fusion protein|protein fusion]] to a [[luminophore]], with subsequent monitoring of the [[protein]]'s [[Protein translocation|translocation]] within a [[Cell (biology)|cell]] as the primary readout for [[drug discovery]] assays.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Life Technologies|url=http://www.bioimage.com/technology.htm|access-date=2017-04-24|website=BioImage|language=en}}</ref>

In December 2010, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced its acquisition of Dionex for $2.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2010-12-13 |title=Thermo Fisher to buy Dionex for $2.1 billion |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-dionex-thermofisher-idUSTRE6BC1K720101213 |access-date=2022-06-01}}</ref>

In May 2011, Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. bought [[Phadia]] to expand into the testing of allergies and [[autoimmune]] diseases for €2.47 billion ($3.5 billion) in cash.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/2011-05-19/thermo-fisher-buys-testing-company-phadia-for-3-5-billion-2-.html | work=Bloomberg | title=Thermo Fisher Rises to Record After $3.5 Billion Phadia Buy}}</ref>

In April 2013, after a competitive bidding with [[Hoffmann-La Roche]],<ref name=Brennan2013>{{cite news | last = Brennan| first = Zachary| date = March 2013| title = Price of Life Tech Steady at $11B as Roche Joins Bidding War| newspaper = Outsourcing-Pharma.com| url = http://www.outsourcing-pharma.com/Preclinical-Research/Price-of-Life-Tech-Steady-at-11B-as-Roche-Joins-Bidding-War-Set-for-April| access-date = 2017-08-03}}</ref> Thermo Fisher acquired [[Life Technologies (Thermo Fisher Scientific)|Life Technologies Corporation]] for [[United States dollar|US$]]13.6 billion in a deal, adding further service lines related to advanced DNA sequencing and [[genetics|genetic]] testing.<ref>{{cite news| url= https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lifetechnologies-thermofisher-idUSBRE93D0A620130415 | title= Thermo Fisher to buy Life Tech for $13.6 billion | author= Bill Berkrot and Susan Kelly | publisher=Reuters | date=15 April 2013}}</ref> Life Technologies was originally formed in 2008 through a $6.7B merger of [[Invitrogen]], a cell therapy, and [[Applied Biosystems]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Applied Biosystems, Invitrogen complete $6.7 billion merger |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/sanfrancisco/stories/2008/11/17/daily103.html |access-date=27 May 2024 |work=www.bizjournals.com |date=21 November 2008}}</ref> The company also acquired GIBCO (Grand Island Biological Company) as part of the Life Technologies acquisition.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Staff |first1=G. E. N. |title=Thermo Fisher Acquiring BD's Advanced Bioprocessing Business |url=https://www.genengnews.com/news/thermo-fisher-acquiring-bds-advanced-bioprocessing-business-2/ |access-date=27 May 2024 |work=GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News |date=7 September 2018}}</ref>

In February 2015, the company announced it would acquire Advanced Scientifics for $300 million in a cash-deal. ASI designs manufactures, and delivers technologies used in bioprocessing.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genengnews.com/gen-news-highlights/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-single-use-specialist-asi-for-300m/81250894/|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires Single-Use Specialist ASI for $300 Million - GEN News Highlights - GEN|work=GEN|date=5 February 2015}}</ref> In June 2015, the company announced its intention to acquire Alfa Aesar, a global manufacturer of research chemicals for $405 million<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.genengnews.com/gen-news-highlights/thermo-fisher-scientific-agrees-to-acquire-research-chemicals-firm/81251436/|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Agrees to Acquire Research Chemicals Firm|work=GEN|date=25 June 2015}}</ref> from [[Johnson Matthey]], and the acquisition was completed at the end of September<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ir.thermofisher.com/investors/news-and-events/news-releases/news-release-details/2015/Thermo-Fisher-Scientific-Completes-Acquisition-of-Alfa-Aesar-to-Significantly-Expand-Laboratory-Chemicals-Offering/default.aspx|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific - Thermo Fisher Scientific Completes Acquisition of Alfa Aesar to Significantly Expand Laboratory Chemicals Offering|access-date=5 January 2016}}</ref>

In January 2016, the company announced it would acquire [[Affymetrix]] for $1.3 billion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genengnews.com/news/thermo-fisher-scientific-to-acquire-affymetrix-for-1-3b/|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to Acquire Affymetrix for $1.3B|first=GEN Staff|last=Writer|date=January 11, 2016}}</ref> On May 27, 2016, the company announced it would acquire [[FEI Company]] for $4.2 billion, a manufacturer of [[electron microscope]]s.<ref>{{Cite news
 |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-05-27/thermo-fisher-scientific-to-buy-fei-for-about-4-2-billion |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to Buy FEI for About $4.2 Billion |last=Hallam |first=Kristen |publisher=Bloomberg |access-date=2016-05-28 |date=27 May 2016 }}</ref> This acquisition is anticipated to close in early 2017 and will contribute to the growth of Thermo's Analytical Instruments business group.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/boston/blog/bioflash/2016/05/thermo-ceo-mum-on-whether-he-had-competitors-in-4.html|title=Thermo CEO mum on whether he had competitors in $4.2B bid for FEI|last=Seiffert|first=Don|date=27 May 2016|work=Boston Business Journal|access-date=31 May 2016}}</ref> In November the company announced it would acquire MTI-GlobalStem, a previously privately held company that develops reagents for cell transfection, neurobiology and stem cell research.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-mti-globalstem|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires MTI-GlobalStem - Thermo Fisher Scientific eNews|website=news.thermofisher.com|access-date=April 4, 2017|archive-date=July 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712122630/http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-mti-globalstem|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2017, the company acquired Finesse Solutions, Inc., developer of scalable control automation systems and software for bioproduction after receiving early termination of the waiting period under the [[Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-receives-early-termination-hart-scott-rodino-waiting-period-a|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Receives Early Termination of Hart-Scott-Rodino Waiting Period for Acquisition of Finesse Solutions, Inc. - Thermo Fisher Scientific eNews|website=news.thermofisher.com|access-date=April 4, 2017|archive-date=April 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170405073702/http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-receives-early-termination-hart-scott-rodino-waiting-period-a|url-status=dead}}</ref> The transaction was completed a day later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-completes-acquisition-finesse-solutions-inc|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Completes Acquisition of Finesse Solutions, Inc. - Thermo Fisher Scientific eNews|website=news.thermofisher.com|access-date=April 4, 2017|archive-date=July 3, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703172549/http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-completes-acquisition-finesse-solutions-inc|url-status=dead}}</ref> In March, the company announced it would acquire Core Informatics, provider of cloud-based platforms supporting scientific data management.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-core-informatics-provider-leading-cloud-based-scient|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires Core Informatics, Provider of Leading Cloud-Based Scientific Data Platforms - Thermo Fisher Scientific eNews|website=news.thermofisher.com|access-date=April 4, 2017|archive-date=July 17, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170717061057/http://news.thermofisher.com/press-release/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-core-informatics-provider-leading-cloud-based-scient|url-status=dead}}</ref> In August, the company acquired Patheon, a [[contract development and manufacturing organization]] serving the pharmaceutical and biotechnology sectors, for approximately $7.2 billion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pharmtech.com/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-patheon|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires Patheon|last=Editorial Staff|first=Pharmaceutical Technology|website=www.pharmtech.com|language=en|access-date=2017-09-12| url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170912191425/http://www.pharmtech.com/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-patheon | archive-date = 12 September 2017 }}</ref> As of 2017, the company had revenues of $20.9 billion, and was a [[Fortune 500]] company.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fortune.com/fortune500/list/|title=Fortune 500 Companies 2018: Who Made the List|website=Fortune|language=en-US|access-date=2018-11-19|archive-date=January 15, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190115060417/http://fortune.com/fortune500/list/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In September 2018, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced it had signed a definitive agreement with [[Becton, Dickinson]] and Company (BDX) to acquire their Advanced Bioprocessing business.  This BD business had annualized revenue of approximately $100 million; as of October 16, 2018, it had been integrated into Thermo Fisher's Life Sciences Solutions Segment.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://markets.businessinsider.com/news/stocks/thermo-fisher-to-acquire-bd-s-advanced-bioprocessing-business-quick-facts-1027516774|title=Thermo Fisher To Acquire BD's Advanced Bioprocessing Business - Quick Facts|first=Thermo Fisher|last=Scientific|website=markets.businessinsider.com|language=en|access-date=2022-08-22}}</ref>

In March 2019, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced its entry into the [[gene therapy]] manufacturing market with a $1.7 billion cash acquisition for Brammer Bio.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/business/2019/03/25/thermo-fisher-gets-into-gene-therapy-with-deal-for-brammer-bio/tZJf1ca7rjvvOBxSafWogN/story.html|title=Thermo Fisher gets into gene therapy with $1.7b deal for Brammer Bio - The Boston Globe|last=Reporter|first=Jonathan Saltzman-|website=BostonGlobe.com|access-date=2019-03-27}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://thermofisher.mediaroom.com/2019-03-24-Thermo-Fisher-Scientific-to-Acquire-Brammer-Bio-a-Leader-in-Viral-Vector-Manufacturing|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to Acquire Brammer Bio, a Leader in Viral Vector Manufacturing|website=MediaRoom|language=en|access-date=2019-03-27|archive-date=November 4, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211104122034/https://thermofisher.mediaroom.com/2019-03-24-Thermo-Fisher-Scientific-to-Acquire-Brammer-Bio-a-Leader-in-Viral-Vector-Manufacturing|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/thermo-fisher-shoulders-into-gene-therapy-manufacturing-1-7b-deal-for-brammer|title=Thermo Fisher shoulders into gene therapy manufacturing with $1.7B deal for Brammer|newspaper=Fierce Pharma|date=25 March 2019 |language=en|access-date=2019-03-27}}</ref> In May 2019, Thermo Fisher Scientific partnered with MMJ International Holdings to manufacture drug products developed by MMJ for the treatment of [[multiple sclerosis]] and [[Huntington's disease]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://multiplesclerosisnewstoday.com/news-posts/2019/08/12/mmj-international-holdings-shipping-thc-and-cbd-to-us-for-clinical-trials/|title=To Support MS Cannabinoid Studies, MMJ Asks US Agency to OK Shipments from Canada|date=2019-08-14|website=Multiple Sclerosis News Today|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-06|last1=Phd |first1=Joana Carvalho }}</ref> In June, the business announced it would acquire mass spectrometry software provider, HighChem.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires HighChem, Provider of Mass Spectrometry Software|url=https://www.biospace.com/article/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-highchem-provider-of-mass-spectrometry-software/|access-date=2020-06-20|website=BioSpace|language=en-US}}</ref>

In March 2020, Thermo Fisher Scientific received [[emergency use authorization]] from the FDA for a test for [[SARS-CoV-2]] to help mitigate the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |last2= |first2= |date=2020-03-14 |title=Thermo Fisher Coronavirus Test Gets FDA Emergency Use Authorization |url=https://www.360dx.com/regulatory-news-fda-approvals/thermo-fisher-coronavirus-test-gets-fda-emergency-use-authorization |access-date=2026-04-22 |website=360Dx |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-03-16 |title=FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization to Thermo Fisher Scientific's Diagnostic Test for COVID-19 {{!}} Pharmaceutical Technology |url=https://www.pharmtech.com/view/fda-issues-emergency-use-authorization-thermo-fisher-scientific-s-diagnostic-test-covid-19 |access-date=2026-04-22 |website=www.pharmtech.com |language=en}}</ref> Thermo Fisher also partnered with its biopharma customers, including Pfizer and Moderna, to
support the development and production of new mRNA-based COVID-19 vaccines.<ref>{{cite news |date=1 June 2021 |title=Moderna partners with Thermo Fisher to scale up Covid vaccine production |url=https://www.cnbc.com/2021/06/01/moderna-partners-with-thermo-fisher-to-scale-covid-vaccine-production-.html |access-date=25 May 2024 |work=CNBC |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Flak |first1=Agnieszka |date=March 25, 2021 |title=Thermo Fisher to work with Pfizer-BioNtech on vaccine production in Italy |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-italy-thermo-fishe/thermo-fisher-to-work-with-pfizer-biontech-on-vaccine-production-in-italy-idUSKBN2BH2SB/ |access-date=25 May 2024}}</ref>

In March 2020, Thermo Fisher Scientific agreed to purchase [[Qiagen]], a molecular diagnostics company, for $10.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Martuscelli|first=Carlo|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/thermo-fisher-to-buy-diagnostic-company-for-10-1-billion-11583236681|title=Thermo Fisher to Buy Diagnostic Company for $10.1 Billion|date=2020-03-03|work=Wall Street Journal|access-date=2020-03-03|language=en-US|issn=0099-9660}}</ref> In July, the offer for Qiagen was raised from €39 to €43 per share (€11.3 billion in total).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-qiagen-m-a-thermo-fisher-idUKKCN24H2A2 |title=Thermo Fisher's sweetened Qiagen bid fails to win over key investor |author=<!--not stated-->|newspaper=Reuters |date=July 16, 2020 |location =www.reuters.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/article/thermo-fisher-scientific-and-qiagen-n-v-agree-on-amended-terms-to-acquisition-agreement/|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific and QIAGEN N.V. Agree on Amended Terms to Acquisition Agreement|website=BioSpace}}</ref>  On August 13, the company announced that its offer to acquire all of the ordinary share had lapsed, and it terminated the acquisition agreement.<ref>{{Cite press release|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thermo-fisher-scientific-announces-results-of-offer-to-acquire-qiagen-lapse-of-offer-and-termination-of-acquisition-agreement-301111751.html|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Announces Results of Offer to Acquire QIAGEN, Lapse of Offer and Termination of Acquisition Agreement|first=Thermo Fisher|last=Scientific|website=www.prnewswire.com}}</ref>

In August 2020, Thermo Fisher Scientific opened its new Lenexa facility aimed at boosting the production and manufacturing of COVID-19 testing supplies.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-08-28|title=Biotech firm Thermo Fisher Scientific opens Lenexa facility aimed at boosting Kansas' COVID-19 testing capacity|url=https://shawneemissionpost.com/2020/08/28/biotech-firm-thermo-fisher-opens-lenexa-facility-aimed-at-boosting-kansas-covid-19-testing-capacity-100046/|access-date=2020-09-10|website=Shawnee Mission Post - Community news and events for northeast Johnson County|language=en-US}}</ref> In December the business announced it would acquire Phitonex, Inc.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/article/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-programmable-dye-platform-pioneer-phitonex/|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires Programmable Dye Platform Pioneer Phitonex|website=BioSpace}}</ref>

In January 2021, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced it had acquired Belgium-based viral vector manufacturer, Henogen SA, from [[Novasep|Groupe Novasep SAS]] for €725 million in cash<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/article/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-viral-vector-manufacturing-business-from-novasep/|title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Acquires Viral Vector Manufacturing Business from Novasep|website=BioSpace}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/article/thermo-fisher-buys-novasep-viral-vector-business-expanding-deeply-into-gene-therapy/|title=Thermo Fisher Takes Deep Dive into Cell and Gene Therapy with Viral Vector Business Buy|website=BioSpace|date=January 15, 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kansteiner |first=Fraiser |date=2021-05-21 |title=Thermo Fisher links up with UCSF on soup-to-nuts cell therapy factory and research center |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/thermo-fisher-links-up-uc-san-francisco-cell-therapy-factory-and-collaboration-center |access-date=2023-09-27 |website=Fierce Pharma}}</ref> and point-of-care molecular diagnostics provider Mesa Biotech, Inc. for up to $550 million.<ref>{{cite news |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to Acquire Point-of-Care Molecular Diagnostics Provider Mesa Biotech |url=https://www.biospace.com/article/thermo-fisher-scientific-to-acquire-point-of-care-molecular-diagnostics-provider-mesa-biotech/ |access-date=27 May 2024 |work=BioSpace |date=19 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Khandekar |first1=Amruta |title=Thermo Fisher buys Henogen for nearly $880 million in gene therapy expansion |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSKBN29K1BL/ |access-date=27 May 2024 |date=15 January 2021}}</ref>

In April 2021, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced the acquisition of [[PPD, Inc.]], a contract research organization, for a total cash purchase price of $17.4 billion-plus the assumption of approximately $3.5 billion of net debt. PPD generated $4.7 billion in revenue during FY 2020, and this transaction, which values their company at approximately $20.9 billion.<ref>{{cite web|date=2021-04-15|title=Thermo Fisher expands pharma service business with $17.4 bln PPD acquisition|url=https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/thermo-fisher-expands-pharma-service-business-with-174-bln-ppd-acquisition-2021-04-15/|work=Reuters|language=en-US}}</ref> In November, the business announced it would acquire [[PharmaFluidics]] and its [[μPAC]] range of micro-chip-based chromatography products.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biospace.com/article/releases/thermo-fisher-scientific-adds-patterned-microchip-based-technology-to-liquid-chromatography-portfolio/?s=79|title = Thermo Fisher Scientific Adds Patterned Microchip-based Technology to Liquid Chromatography Portfolio| date=November 2021 }}</ref>

In January 2022, Thermo Fisher Scientific acquired PeproTech, a developer and manufacturer of recombinant proteins, for $1.85 billion. PeproTech became part of Thermo Fisher’s biosciences business and was integrated into the Life Sciences Solutions Segment.<ref>{{cite news |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific acquires PeproTech for $1.85bn |url=https://www.medicaldevice-network.com/news/thermo-fisher-scientific-acquires-peprotech/ |access-date=27 May 2024 |work=Medical Device Network |date=6 January 2022}}</ref>

In October 2022, the company agreed to buy British diagnostics firm, The Binding Site Group, in an all-cash deal for US$2.6{{nbsp}}billion from [[Nordic Capital]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/thermo-fisher-buy-diagnostics-firm-binding-site-26-bln-2022-10-31/ |title=Thermo Fisher to buy diagnostics firm Binding Site for $2.6 bln |date=2022-10-31 |last1=Leo |first1=Leroy |last2=Jain |first2=Pratik |work=[[Reuters]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-10-30/thermo-fisher-said-to-near-2-3-billion-deal-for-binding-site |title=Thermo Fisher to buy UK's Binding Site in $2.6 billion deal |date=2022-10-30 |last1=Foerster |first1=Jan-Henrik |last2=Davis |first2=Michelle F |work=[[Bloomberg News]] |url-access=limited}}</ref> The acquisition completed in January 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-03 |title=Thermo Fisher completes $2.8bn acquisition of The Binding Site Group |url=https://www.nsmedicaldevices.com/news/thermo-fisher-acquires-the-binding-site-group/ |access-date=2023-01-03 |website=NS Medical Devices |language=en-US}}</ref>

In July 2023, the business announced it would acquire CorEvitas, LLC from Audax Private Equity for more than $900 million in cash.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.biospace.com/article/releases/thermo-fisher-scientific-to-acquire-corevitas-/?s=79 | title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to Acquire CorEvitas | date=July 6, 2023 }}</ref> In August 2023, it was announced Thermo Fisher had completed the acquisition for $912.5 million (in cash).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mireku |first=Akosua |date=2023-08-15 |title=Thermo Fisher completes $912.5m acquisition of CorEvitas |url=https://www.pharmaceutical-technology.com/news/thermo-fisher-corevitas-acquisition/ |access-date=2023-08-15 |website=Pharmaceutical Technology |language=en-US}}</ref>

In October 2023, Thermo Fisher Scientific acquired Olink Holding for $3.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-10-17 |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific to buy Olink in $3.1 billion deal |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/deals/thermo-fisher-scientific-buy-olink-31-billion-deal-2023-10-17/ |access-date=2023-10-23}}</ref>

In February 2025, Thermo Fisher announced the acquisition of Solventum’s purification and filtration business for $4.1 billion.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Liu |first=Angus |date=2025-02-25 |title=Thermo Fisher buys 3M spinoff's filtration unit for $4.1B |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/41b-deal-thermo-fisher-buys-3m-spinoffs-filtration-unit-beef-bioproduction |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=www.fiercepharma.com |language=en}}</ref>

The transaction was expected to close mid-2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marchese |first=Adriano |date=2025-10-29 |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific Agrees to Buy Clario Holdings for $8.88 Billion |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/energy-oil/thermo-fisher-scientific-agrees-to-buy-clario-holdings-for-8-88-billion-adb1875b |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Leadership==
Marc N. Casper has been Chief Executive Officer of Thermo Fisher Scientific since October 2009, and was elected Chairman of the Board in February 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=This Top CEO's Rock-Solid Company Acts Like A Teenager |url=https://www.investors.com/news/management/leaders-and-success/thermo-fisher-scientific-ceo-acts-like-company-half-its-age/ |access-date=27 May 2024 |work=Investor's Business Daily |date=23 December 2020}}</ref> He also served as President from 2009 until March 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kellaher |first=Colin |date=2026-01-12 |title=Thermo Fisher Chief Operating Officer Michel Lagarde Leaving Company |url=https://www.wsj.com/business/c-suite/thermo-fisher-chief-operating-officer-michel-lagarde-leaving-company-91815ec8 |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=The Wall Street Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> He joined the company in 2001 as President of the Life Sciences sector of Thermo Electron. Casper was named Senior Vice President in 2003, and in 2005 assumed responsibility for all of the company’s operating divisions. After the merger creating Thermo Fisher Scientific in 2006, he was named Executive Vice President and President of its Analytical Technologies business, and in 2008 he became the company’s Chief Operating Officer.

Prior to joining Thermo Fisher, Casper served as President, Chief Executive Officer and a Director of Kendro Laboratory Products. Previously, he worked for clinical diagnostics provider Dade Behring Inc., serving as President–Americas. He began his career as a strategy consultant at Bain & Company and later joined Bain Capital.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kuehner-Hebert |first=Katie |date=2020-06-21 |title=CEO of the Week: Thermo Fisher Scientific's Marc N. Casper |url=https://chiefexecutive.net/ceo-of-the-week-thermo-fisher-scientifics-marc-n-casper/ |access-date=2026-06-30 |website=ChiefExecutive.net |language=en-US}}</ref> 

==Partnerships==
In September 2017, Thermo Fisher Scientific signed an agreement with the Institute of Pathology Heidelberg (IPH) to establish its Center of Molecular Pathology at [[Heidelberg University]] Hospital as the newest member of the Next Generation Sequencing Companion Dx Center of Excellence Program (COEP). The initiative focuses on establishing strategic collaborations with leading, European-based organizations that can lead studies using Thermo Fisher's Oncomine portfolio of research panels destined for development as companion diagnostics to help drive precision [[oncology]] in the region.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.technologynetworks.com/tn/news/institute-of-pathology-joins-thermo-fisher-scientific-to-drive-oncology-companion-diagnostic-291618|title=Institute of Pathology Joins Thermo Fisher Scientific to Drive Oncology Companion Diagnostic Development|work=Technology Networks|access-date=2017-09-12}}</ref>

In 2021, Thermo Fisher announced the construction of a cell therapy development, manufacturing and collaboration center in cooperation with [[University of California, San Francisco]] on the school's Mission Bay campus.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kansteiner |first=Fraiser |date=2023-08-29 |title=Drugs from J&J, Merck, Novartis, BMS and more set for first round of Medicare price negotiations: CMS |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/pharma/medicare-unveils-list-10-drugs-set-price-negotiations-under-ira |access-date=2023-08-31}}</ref>

In February 2022, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced a 15-year strategic collaboration
agreement with Moderna, Inc. The collaboration was designed to scale up the
manufacturing of Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine and other investigational mRNA
products.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Kansteiner |first1=Fraiser |title=MANUFACTURING Moderna taps Thermo Fisher for 15-year mRNA production pact for COVID vaccines and more |url=https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/moderna-taps-thermo-fisher-for-15-year-mrna-production-pact-including-covid-19 |access-date=25 May 2024 |date=Feb 23, 2022}}</ref>

In May 2023, Thermo Fisher partnered with [[Pfizer]], with plans to work together on expanding testing capabilities for lung and breast cancer patients.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-10 |title=Thermo Fisher (TMO) Partners With Pfizer to Expand NGS Testing |url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/thermo-fisher-tmo-partners-pfizer-132301690.html |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=Yahoo Finance |language=en-US}}</ref>

In November 2023, Thermo Fisher partnered with [[Flagship Pioneering]], a biotechnology company.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hale |first=Conor |date=28 November 2023 |title=Thermo Fisher teams up with Flagship Pioneering to forge new life science tool startups |url=https://www.fiercebiotech.com/medtech/thermo-fisher-teams-flagship-forge-new-life-science-tool-startups |access-date=30 January 2024 |website=Fierce Biotech}}</ref> Together, they plan to create companies in the biotechnology field.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Khalil |first=Kiays |date=2023-11-30 |title=Thermo Fisher and Flagship Pioneering partner to establish platform companies |url=https://www.medicaldevice-network.com/news/thermo-fisher-and-flagship-pioneering-partner-to-establish-platform-companies/ |access-date=2024-01-30 |website=Medical Device Network |language=en-US}}</ref>

In January 2025, Thermo Fisher partnered with the UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project (UKB-PPP) to support the world’s largest human proteomics study. Using the Olink Explore platform, UKB-PPP seeks to analyze more than 5,400 proteins from 600,000 samples to fuel the discovery of new protein biomarkers that can be used to predict, diagnose, and treat diseases.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Research & Development |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific's Olink platform selected for world's largest human proteome study |url=https://manufacturingchemist.com/thermo-fisher-scientific-s-olink-platform-selected-for-world-s |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=manufacturingchemist.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Unlocking the Human Proteome |url=http://www.technologynetworks.com/proteomics/blog/unlocking-the-human-proteome-397650 |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=Proteomics & Metabolomics from Technology Networks |language=en}}</ref>

In February 2025, Thermo Fisher entered a 10-year virtual power purchase agreement (VPPA) with X-ELIO to secure 118 megawatts of solar energy, moving its European operations closer to a 100% renewable electricity goal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Temporal |first=Rhiannon |date=2025-02-05 |title=Thermo Fisher Scientific announces 10-year VPPA with X-ELIO |url=https://pharmaceuticalmanufacturer.media/api/content/24586c60-e3d2-11ef-bfb4-12163087a831/ |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=European Pharmaceutical Manufacturer |language=en-gb}}</ref>

In June 2025, Thermo Fisher partnered with the Regeneron Genetics Center which selected the Olink Explore platform for large-scale proteomics investigation involving nearly 200,000 patient samples aiming to unlock new insights into the dynamic biology and mechanisms of human disease.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Regeneron Genetics Center Selects Olink® Explore HT for Landmark Proteomics Study of 200,000 Patient Samples |url=http://www.technologynetworks.com/proteomics/product-news/regeneron-genetics-center-selects-olink-explore-ht-for-landmark-proteomics-study-of-200000-patient-401103 |access-date=2025-08-21 |website=Proteomics & Metabolomics from Technology Networks |language=en}}</ref>

== Controversies ==
 
=== Xinjiang and Tibet ===
{{Further|Persecution of Uyghurs in China|Human rights in Tibet}}
In February 2019, Thermo Fisher Scientific announced that it would stop selling its equipment in [[Xinjiang]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Wee|first=Sui-Lee|date=2019-02-21|title=China Uses DNA to Track Its People, With the Help of American Expertise|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/02/21/business/china-xinjiang-uighur-dna-thermo-fisher.html|access-date=2020-06-20|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> In June 2020, Thermo Fisher Scientific was reported to sell its equipment to security services in China for use in what was alleged as part of a genetic surveillance program.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Wee|first=Sui-Lee|date=2020-06-17|title=China Is Collecting DNA From Tens of Millions of Men and Boys, Using U.S. Equipment|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/17/world/asia/China-DNA-surveillance.html|access-date=2020-06-17|issn=0362-4331}}</ref> A report from the [[Australian Strategic Policy Institute]] found that Thermo Fisher Scientific collaborated with the Chinese [[Ministry of Public Security (China)|Ministry of Public Security]] to develop a Huaxia PCR amplification kit specifically to identify the genotypes of [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]], [[Tibetan people|Tibetan]] and [[Hui people|Hui]] ethnic minorities.<ref>{{Cite web|last2=Leibold|first2=James |last1=Dirks|first1=Emile |title=Genomic surveillance|url=https://www.aspi.org.au/report/genomic-surveillance|access-date=2020-10-04|website=www.aspi.org.au|date=June 16, 2020 |language=en}}</ref> In June 2021, ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that, despite bans, Thermo Fisher Scientific equipment continued to be sold to police in Xinjiang.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Wee|first=Sui-Lee|date=2021-06-11|title=China Still Buys American DNA Equipment for Xinjiang Despite Blocks|language=en-US|work=[[The New York Times]]|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/06/11/business/china-dna-xinjiang-american.html|access-date=2021-06-30|issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

In 2022, following reports that Thermo Fisher Scientific had sold products to police in the [[Tibet Autonomous Region]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hvistendahl |first=Mara |date=September 13, 2022 |title=Tibetan Police Bought Thermo Fisher DNA Equipment, Chinese Government Documents Show |url=https://theintercept.com/2022/09/13/china-tibet-police-dna-thermo-fisher/ |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=[[The Intercept]] |language=en}}</ref> the [[Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China]] called on governments to "investigate and suspend commercial activities with companies providing the PRC government with technologies to carry out biometric surveillance in the Uyghur Region, Tibet and elsewhere in the PRC, including the PRC state backed [[BGI Group]] and US firm Thermo Fisher."<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Operations |first1=Andrew |date=2022-12-16 |title=Legislators call for sanctions on firms complicit in mass DNA harvesting of Tibetans and Uyghurs |url=https://ipac.global/legislators-call-for-sanctions-on-firms-complicit-in-mass-dna-harvesting-of-tibetans-and-uyghurs/ |access-date=2023-03-19 |website=[[Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> Thermo Fisher Scientific subsequently halted sales of DNA collection kits in Tibet.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Allen-Ebrahimian |first=Bethany |date=January 3, 2024 |title=Thermo Fisher halts DNA collection kit sales in Tibet |work=[[Axios (website)|Axios]] |url=https://www.axios.com/2024/01/03/tibet-thermo-fisher-halts-dna-collection-kit-sales |access-date=January 3, 2024}}</ref>

=== HeLa cells ===
In October 2021 the estate of [[Henrietta Lacks]] sued to get past and future payment for the alleged and widely known unauthorized sale by Thermo Fisher Scientific of her [[HeLa]] cells which are essential in many types of research.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Estate of Henrietta Lacks sues Thermo Fisher over the improper sale of her immortal cells |url=https://endpoints.news/estate-of-henrietta-lacks-sues-thermo-fisher-over-the-improper-sale-of-her-immortal-cells/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Endpoints News |language=en}}</ref> Over 50 million tons of her cells have been produced and used in over 60,000 scientific studies touching virtually every realm of medicine, including the development of [[polio vaccines]], [[gene mapping]], [[in-vitro fertilization]], and multitudes more.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zielinski |first=Sarah |title=Henrietta Lacks’ ‘Immortal’ Cells |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/henrietta-lacks-immortal-cells-6421299/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Smithsonian Magazine |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iflscience.com/health-and-medicine/henrietta-lacks-descendants-sue-company-they-believe-profits-from-her-immortal-cells/|title=Henrietta Lacks' Descendants Sue Company They Believe Profits From Her Immortal Cells|website=IFLScience|date=6 October 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/oct/04/henrietta-lacks-estate-sues-pharmaceutical-cells|title = Henrietta Lacks' estate sues drug company that sold her cells|website = [[TheGuardian.com]]|date = 4 October 2021}}</ref>

In May 2022, it was announced Thermo Fisher Scientific went to court to seek a dismissal of the lawsuit.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-05-17 |title=Thermo Fisher seeks dismissal of Henrietta Lacks' family's lawsuit regarding sale of her cells |url=https://www.wgbh.org/news/local-news/2022/05/17/thermo-fisher-seeks-dismissal-of-henrietta-lacks-familys-lawsuit-regarding-sale-of-her-cells |access-date=2022-06-16 |website=News |language=en}}</ref> In late July 2023, with the motion to dismiss still outstanding, the court ordered the parties to attend a settlement conference.<ref>{{cite news |title=Henrietta Lacks family lawsuit against biotech company ordered to go to settlement conference next week |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/health/bs-md-lacks-lawsuit-settlement-conference-scheduled-20230728-q4tzrzensff3zfflkku5smj3xu-story.html |work=Baltimore Sun |date=28 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Family of Henrietta Lacks asks court to reject Thermo Fisher's second motion to dismiss lawsuit |url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/health/bs-hs-henrietta-lacks-response-brief-20230222-pdj3anxw2rbflhmtoo3dw64sai-story.html |work=Baltimore Sun |date=22 February 2023}}</ref> Soon after that, settlement of the suit, with undisclosed terms, was announced.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holpuch |first1=Amanda |title=Family of Henrietta Lacks Settles With Biotech Company That Used Her Cells |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2023/08/01/science/henrietta-lacks-cells-lawsuit-settlement.html |work=The New York Times |date=1 August 2023}}</ref>

=== Mexican plant ===
In 2013, Opengate Capital Group LLC filed suit against Thermo Fisher Scientific for selling it a manufacturing plant controlled by the [[Gulf Cartel]]. According to Opengate Capital, the company withheld important documents and pressured employees into concealing the presence of the drug cartel.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Walker|first=Joseph|date=2013-05-11|title=Thermo Sold Plant Overrun by Drug Cartel, Suit Alleges|language=en-US|work=Wall Street Journal|url=https://online.wsj.com/article/SB10001424127887323744604578475692965871134.html|access-date=2022-02-05|issn=0099-9660}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2013-05-11|title=Thermo Fisher sued over sale of Mexico plant used by drug cartel|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/thermofisher-lawsuit-opengate-idUSL2N0DS0H520130511|access-date=2022-02-05}}</ref>

=== Image manipulation ===
In May 2026, scientists found that a large number of images from Thermo Fisher Scientific's catalog had been manipulated, with sections of the images blanked out and duplicated with the same part of the picture copied into multiple places.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Garisto |first=Dan |date=2026-05-29 |title=Science sleuths uncover more than 100 suspicious images in Thermo Fisher antibody catalogue |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-026-01706-2 |journal=Nature |language=en |doi=10.1038/d41586-026-01706-2 |pmid=42225798 |issn=1476-4687}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Reese |first1=Richardson |last2=Sholto |first2=David |title=Problematic images in vendor antibody verification data |url=https://zenodo.org/records/20402476 |journal=Zenodo |date=2026 |language=en |doi=10.5281/zenodo.20402476 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260530021111/https://zenodo.org/records/20402476 |archive-date=2026-05-30}}</ref> The images were claimed to validate the effectiveness of antibody products which have uses including [[Western blot]]s.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Oldach |first1=Laurel |title=Sleuths say Thermo Fisher doctored data to sell antibodies |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/104/web/2026/05/Sleuths-say-Thermo-Fisher-doctored.html |website=Chemical & Engineering News |publisher=American Chemical Society |access-date=16 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Richardson |first1=Reese |title=How much of Thermo Fisher's antibody data has been manipulated? |url=https://reeserichardson.blog/2026/05/28/how-much-of-thermo-fishers-antibody-data-has-been-manipulated/ |website=Reese Richardson |access-date=16 June 2026}}</ref>

extract:
Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is an American life science and clinical research company. It is a global supplier of analytical instruments, clinical development solutions, specialty diagnostics, laboratory, pharmaceutical and biotechnology services. Based in Waltham, Massachusetts, Thermo Fisher was formed through the merger of Thermo Electron and Fisher Scientific in 2006. Thermo Fisher Scientific has acquired other reagent, consumable, instrumentation, and service providers, including Life Technologies Corporation (2013), Alfa Aesar (2015), Affymetrix (2016), FEI Company (2016), BD Advanced Bioprocessing (2018), and PPD (2021).
It ranked 106th on the Fortune 500 list based on its 2025 annual revenue of $44.556 billion.
